chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from 'Umar ibn Aban, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about what the people are saying, that a sealed scroll was handed over to Umm Salamah. So he said: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was taken, 'Ali عليه السلام inherited his knowledge, his weapons, and what was there. Then it passed to al-Hasan, then it passed to al-Husayn عليه السلام.
He said: I said: Then it passed to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, then it passed to his son, then it came to you? He said: Yes.

key_terms.انْتَهَى: ended up; arrived finally in the possession of the addressed Imam
key_terms.سِلَاحَهُ: his weapons; the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله arms as symbols of authority and inheritance
key_terms.صَارَ: passed on; moved in succession from one Imam to the next
key_terms.صَحِيفَةٌ مَخْتُومَةٌ: a sealed scroll or written document mentioned in the report being discussed
key_terms.عِلْمَهُ: his knowledge; the divinely entrusted knowledge of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.قُبِضَ: was taken; a reverential expression for the passing of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.وَرِثَ: inherited; received by succession after the passing of the previous holder

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the transfer of the Messenger of Allah’s صلى الله عليه وآله knowledge and weapons to the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the knowledge, weapons, and entrusted possessions of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله passed in succession through Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali عليه السلام and then through the Imams عليهم السلام. It highlights the continuity of religious authority and inherited sacred trust within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
